samples.summary: New 403-specific error message in DocumentAnalyticsPage has no test
samples.evidence: The diff adds a distinct rendering branch: `error instanceof HttpError && error.status === 403` renders a permission-specific message instead of "Failed to load analytics." No test exercises either branch. There is no test file for document-analytics.tsx (globbed packages/frontend/src/app/analytics/** — only date-range.test.ts, format.test.ts, series.test.ts, views-trend-chart.test.tsx exist), and the new test added by this PR (packages/frontend/src/app/workspaces/__tests__/workspace-analytics.test.tsx) covers only the ranking page. So nothing verifies that getDocumentAnalytics actually surfaces an `HttpError` instance with `.status === 403` through react-query (it goes through `assertOk` in api/http-error.ts and `fetchWithAuth`); if the thrown error were wrapped or a different class, the page would silently keep showing the generic text and every suite would still be green.

samples.summary: No test for the warehouse-row-without-Postgres-doc fallback (`d?.authorID ?? null`, title fallback)
samples.evidence: The controller now handles a missing Postgres row via `d?.title ?? r.documentId` and `d?.authorID ?? null`. The spec fixture (analytics.controller.spec.ts:343-352) always returns matching docs for both warehouse rows, so the undefined-`d` path — which decides both the title fallback and canManage for orphaned/legacy rows (isDocumentManager with authorID null only grants owners) — is never executed. A regression there (e.g. `d!.authorID`) would pass CI.

samples.summary: documentRows now emits canManage:false but no warehouse-level test asserts the placeholder
samples.evidence: The service change adds `canManage: false` as a placeholder that the controller overwrites. No test in the analytics suite asserts the warehouse's own row shape for this field (the controller spec supplies its own hand-built rows), so the placeholder is only covered transitively by type-checking. Low value, noted for completeness.

verdict.reason: The 403-specific branch is real and new: document-analytics.tsx:59-69 renders a permission-specific message when `error instanceof HttpError && error.status === 403`, else "Failed to load analytics."; the task doc (20260809-analytics-details-permission-todo.md:31) lists it as a deliverable of this change and its only test checklist item (line 32) is a backend ranking unit test. I searched far beyond the reviewer's paths and found no test exercising either branch: the second frontend test tree packages/frontend/tests/** (144 test files) has zero matches for "analytics"; repo-wide grep shows App.tsx:50-51 is the only importer of the page and no test file imports App; only 4 frontend tests mention analytics and none render DocumentAnalyticsPage — workspace-analytics.test.tsx:70-81 asserts link visibility on the ranking page only, src/api/analytics.test.ts:4-21 covers only visitor/session id helpers, and tests/api/http-error.test.ts:92-100 tests HttpError construction generically without ever showing that getDocumentAnalytics surfaces an HttpError with status 403. No e2e tree exists. So a user-visible behavior change ships with no meaningful test at all — major under the test-adequacy rubric, and in lane (missing test, not correctness of the branch).
